question: what are the next steps after I finish creating dialog skill steps?

answers: After finishing the creation of a dialog skill, the next steps would be to integrate it with websites or channels that your customers already use, such as Slack. As traffic increases between the assistant and your customers, you can use the analytics tools provided to analyze real conversations and identify areas for improvement. Additionally, you can complete follow-on tutorials to build more advanced dialogs, such as adding more dialog nodes to design complex conversational exchanges.

history.content: Is it possible to build a dialog skill in a language other than English?

Yes, it is possible to build a dialog skill in a language other than English. When creating a dialog skill, you have the option to choose a language other than English from a list if the dialog you plan to build will use a different language.
how do I interate the assistant into my dialogue?

To integrate the assistant into your dialogue, you can follow these steps:
1. Click the Assistants icon to open a list of your assistants.
2. Find the desired assistant and open it.
3. Test your assistant with Preview.
4. Copy the URL from Share this link and use it in a new tab. You can start submitting messages to see how your assistant responds.
5. Type hello into the text field, and watch your assistant respond.
6. After testing, close the web page. Click the X to close the preview link integration page.
Who will build your assistant because I want to pick my assistant's areas of expertise?

You can assemble a team with people who understand your customers and their needs to build your assistant. These subject matter experts can focus on designing an engaging conversational flow. You can decide what you want your assistant to specialize in by reviewing any support call logs that you have access to.
I want to add support for global audiences in case the assistant our team builds will be used globally.

Yes, you can add support for global audiences when building your assistant. There are two approaches you can consider:
1. Quickest solution: The simplest way to add language support is to author the conversational skill in a single language.
2. Most precise solution: If you have the time and resources, the best user experience can be achieved when you build multiple conversational skills, one for each language that you want to support.

Duration 

This tutorial will take approximately 30 minutes to complete.





 Prerequisite 

Before you begin, complete the [Getting Started tutorial](https://cloud.ibm.com/docs/assistant?topic=assistant-getting-started). You will use the Watson Assistant tutorial skill that you created, and add nodes to the simple dialog that you built as part of the getting started exercise.

You can also start with a new dialog skill if you want. Just be sure to create the skill before you begin this tutorial.







 Step 1: Add intents and examples 

Add an intent on the Intents tab. An intent is the purpose or goal that is expressed in user input. You will add a #reservation intent that recognizes user input that indicates that the user wants to make a restaurant reservation.



1. From the Intents page of the tutorial skill, click Add intent.
2. Add the following intent name, and then click Create intent:

reservation

After you identify the list of steps, you can then focus on writing engaging content to turn each interaction into a positive experience for your customer.

![Diagram of a simple exchange between a customer and an actions skill step.](https://cloud.ibm.com/docs-content/v1/content/417db917d18067d9dcc4cf2612564a9a87c3ddc8/assistant/images/action-skill-explained.png)





 Dialog skill 

A dialog skill contains the training data and logic that enables an assistant to help your customers. It contains the following types of artifacts:

You created a simple conversation with two intents and a dialog to recognize them.







 Next steps 

This tutorial is built around a simple example. For a real application, you need to define some more interesting intents, some entities, and a more complex dialog that uses them both. When you have a polished version of the assistant, you can make API calls to it from your client application.



* Complete follow-on tutorials that build more advanced dialogs:



* Add standard nodes with the [Building a complex dialog](https://cloud.ibm.com/docs/assistant-data?topic=assistant-data-tutorial) tutorial.
* Learn about slots with the [Adding a node with slots](https://cloud.ibm.com/docs/assistant-data?topic=assistant-data-tutorial-slots) tutorial.



* Check out more [sample apps](https://cloud.ibm.com/docs/assistant-data?topic=assistant-data-sample-apps) to get ideas.
